
```{r, echo = FALSE, results = "hide", message = FALSE}
library(randomNames)
library(tidyverse)

# Values
name <- randomNames(which.names = "first")
rolls <- sort(sample(2:12, 20, replace = TRUE))
roll_tab <- rolls |>
  table() |>
  as.data.frame()

freq_678 <- roll_tab$Freq[roll_tab$rolls %in% c(6, 7, 8)]

## Solution
res <- sum(freq_678) / sum(roll_tab$Freq) * 100

## Plot
palette <- sample(palette.colors(palette = "Polychrome 36"), 1)

plt <-
  ggplot(mapping = aes(x = rolls)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 1, colour = "black", fill = palette) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2, 12, by = 1)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, max(rolls), by = 1)) +
  xlab("Roll Total") +
  ylab("Frequency") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    axis.text = element_text(size = 16),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 16)
  )

# Save and load plot in temp dir
fn <- "item_5"
path <- file.path("items/rexams", paste0(fn, "_assets"))

# Ensure matching tmp dir exists
dir.create(path, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

ggsave(
  file.path(path, paste0(fn, ".svg")),
  plot = plt,
  units = "cm",
  width = 12,
  height = 8
)

include_supplement(paste0(fn, ".svg"), dir = path)
```

Question
========
`r name` rolled two six-sided die and plotted their values on the histogram below. What percentage of the rolls were either a 6, 7, or 8?

![](item_5.svg)


Solution
========
Each bar shows the number of times a certain value was rolled. Therefore the total percentage of rolls for 6, 7, and 8 is . . .

$$
\begin{align}
\text{Percent} &=
\frac{`r paste(freq_678, collapse = "+")`}{`r paste(roll_tab$Freq, collapse = "+")`} \times 100 \\[0.5em]
&= \frac{`r sum(freq_678)`}{`r sum(roll_tab$Freq)`} \times 100 \\[0.5em]
&= `r fmt(res, 2)`
\end{align}
$$

<br>

**R Code:**

```r
freq_678 <- c(`r paste(freq_678, collapse = ", ")`)
freq_tot <- c(`r paste(roll_tab$Freq, collapse = ", ")`)

sum(freq_678) / sum(freq_tot) * 100
```
